name: Wyze Plug (US)

radios.note: 2.4 GHz Wi-Fi only; Wyze says it won't join 5 GHz. This record is the original WLPP1. The later WLPP1CFH revision sets up over Bluetooth, per FCC filings and the Wyze forum; Wyze's product page doesn't give a model number.

matter.note: Wyze's product page and integrations list name Alexa, Google Assistant and IFTTT and don't mention Matter. That's an absence, not an explicit no, and we found no CSA listing for a Wyze plug.

apple_home.note: Wyze's integration list (Alexa, Google Assistant, IFTTT) leaves out HomeKit, but Wyze never says it's unsupported. No Matter listing found either.

google_home.note: Link your Wyze account in the Google Home app. Wyze says the Google integration is officially supported in the US only.

alexa.note: Through the Wyze Alexa skill; on/off by voice using the plug's name.

smartthings.note: Wyze's integration list (Alexa, Google Assistant, IFTTT) leaves out SmartThings, but Wyze never says it's unsupported.

home_assistant.note: There is no official Wyze integration in Home Assistant. Community custom integrations (e.g. ha-wyzeapi) exist and use the Wyze cloud API.

hubRequired.note: Connects directly to Wi-Fi; Wyze says no hub is needed.

localControl.note: Wyze says the side button still works when Wi-Fi is down, but app control stops. We found no official statement on local network control without the Wyze cloud.

energyMonitoring.note: Wyze says it can't report energy use; the app only shows run time. Wyze's metering plug is the Wyze Plug Outdoor.

maxLoadWatts.note: Wyze lists 100–120 VAC, 60 Hz, 15 A maximum but no watt figure. 15 A at 120 V would be 1800 W; that's derived, not stated.

summary: Alexa and Google Home, yes; Apple Home and SmartThings, not on Wyze's list. The Wyze Plug (WLPP1) links to both assistants through your Wyze account and joins 2.4 GHz Wi-Fi directly, so there's no hub. Wyze names no Matter support. It's a US plug rated 15 A, and it doesn't measure energy: the app only shows how long it ran. Home Assistant has no official Wyze integration.
caveats: 2.4 GHz Wi-Fi only; Wyze says it won't connect to 5 GHz.
Wyze says its Google Assistant integration is officially supported in the US only.
No energy monitoring; the Wyze app only tracks run time.
Home Assistant works only through unofficial community integrations that use the Wyze cloud.
This record covers the original WLPP1; a later revision, WLPP1CFH, sets up over Bluetooth.
